To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DC-SIGNR homozygous 5/5 genotype confers protection against HIV-1 infection, and the 8/5 genotype may be associated with susceptibility of HIV-1 in north Indian population.
DC-SIGN and DCSIGNR polymorphisms are not significantly associated with HIV-1 resistance.
the homozygous DC-SINGR 5/4 genotype is a potential genetic risk factor of HIV-1 transmission in North Indian population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first genetic association study of DC-SIGNR gene polymorphism and HIV-1 infection.
the identification of the role of DC-SIGNR polymorphism in HIV- 1 infection and resistance.
the role of DC-SIGNR polymorphism in HIV- 1-exposed seropositive individuals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the homozygous 5/5 genotype of DC-SIGNR polymorphism confers resistance against HIV-1 infection.
DC-SIGNR homozygosity (5/5) is a potential genetic factor for resistance to HIV-1 in North Indians.
DC-SIGNR genotype is not associated with the risk of HIV-10 infection, but the DC-SIGNR homozygous 5/5 tandem repeat polymorphism is associated with reduced risk of HIV infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DC-SIGNR polymorphisms are associated with HIV-1 infection.
the homozygous DC-SINGR 5/ 5 tandem repeat polymorphism may be associated with HIV-1 resistance.
the homozygous DC-SIGNR 5/5 tandem repeat polymorphism is significantly associated with reduced risk of HIV infection in HIV- exposed seronegative North Indians.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DC-SIGNR polymorphism is significantly associated with HIV-1 resistance and may be a potential genetic factor in HIV-1 resistance in Indian population.
homozygosity of 5/5 tandem repeat polymorphism in neck region of DC-SIGNR gene is associated with reduced risk of HIV transmission in HIV-1 exposed seronegative North Indians.
homozygous 5/5 genotype of DC-SIGNR is significantly associated with HIV-1 resistance in Indian population.
